title: Rightmost Leaf in Last Level of Complete Tree
statement:
You are given a **complete binary tree** with `n` nodes. In a complete binary tree every level is completely filled except possibly the last one, and the nodes of the last level are packed as far to the left as possible.

Find the **rightmost node on the last (deepest) level** of the tree and print its value.

The tree is described by explicit child links. The nodes are numbered `0` to `n - 1` and node `0` is the root. For every node you are given its value and the indices of its left and right child, with `-1` meaning there is no such child. Node numbers carry no ordering information: the numbering is arbitrary, so the node with the largest number is generally not the answer.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked for the optimal solution. A full traversal is O(n); using the fact that the tree is complete, the answer can be found in O(log² n) steps once the tree is built. You were then also asked how you would find the rightmost node of the last level in an arbitrary binary tree (the answer: a level-order traversal, keeping the last node of the final level).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines describes node `i` (for `i = 0 ... n - 1`) with three integers: `value[i]`, `left[i]`, `right[i]`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the value of the rightmost node on the last level.
constraints: -1 ≤ left[i], right[i] < n; node 0 is the root
The input is guaranteed to be a valid complete binary tree

examples.explanation: The root (value 10) has children 20 (node 3) and 30 (node 1). Node 3 has children 40 and 50, and node 1 has the single left child 60. The last level holds 40, 50, 60 from left to right, so the answer is 60.
A single node is the root and also the whole last level.
The last level (depth 2) contains only node 3 with value 4, the left child of node 1. The leaf with value 3 is on a shallower level, so it is not the answer.

complexity.time: O(log^2 n) to find the node, O(n) to read the input

hints: Walk down the left children from the root to learn the depth h of the last level.

The last level can hold up to 2^h nodes, and in a complete tree the nodes that are present form a prefix of those positions. Position j can be reached from the root by following the binary digits of j (0 = left, 1 = right).

Binary search for the largest position j in [0, 2^h - 1] whose root-to-position path exists. Each check costs O(h), so the total is O(log^2 n). A plain BFS that remembers the last node it visits is also fine for passing the tests.
